intro: Work through the tasks in order in TensorFlow Playground, which opens in a new tab with the settings for each task. Think about each question; you do not need to write answers down. Stay on the tasks until the time is up.
playground_note: TensorFlow Playground (github.com/tensorflow/playground) by D. Smilkov, S. Carter and colleagues, Apache License 2.0. By default ("playground_source": "local") Study Mode opens the pinned, offline copy served with DL-VizLab from playground/ (commit 02469bd, see public/playground/NOTICE.md), so the C2 baseline is fixed and needs no network. Set "playground_source" to "hosted" to use playground.tensorflow.org instead.

tasks.title: A single neuron
steps: The network has no hidden layer: the two inputs X₁ and X₂ feed one output neuron directly.
Press the step button (▶|) a few times. Hover over each connection line from an input to the output and note its weight.
Press play (▶) and let it run for about 100 epochs. Watch how the coloured background (the decision boundary) changes.
questions: How does the output neuron combine X₁ and X₂ before applying its activation?
Why is the boundary between the two colours a straight line?

tasks.title: Activation functions
steps: The activation is set to Linear. Press play for about 200 epochs and note the test loss.
Reset (↺), change Activation to Tanh, and play again. Then try ReLU and Sigmoid.
questions: Why can the linear network not separate the circle?
Which activations output only positive values, and which output zero for negative inputs?

tasks.title: Forward propagation
steps: Play for about 100 epochs, then pause.
Hover over each hidden neuron: the small picture shows what it outputs for every point in the plane.
Compare the hidden neurons' pictures with the output picture.
questions: How is the output picture built from the hidden neurons' pictures?

tasks.title: Loss
steps: Tick "Show test data". Play for about 300 epochs and watch "Training loss" and "Test loss" under the output.
Reset and increase "Ratio of training to test data" to 90 %, then play again.
questions: Why can the training loss be lower than the test loss?

tasks.title: Gradient descent and the learning rate
steps: With learning rate 0.003, play for 100 epochs and note the loss.
Reset, set the learning rate to 0.03, and repeat. Then try 3 and finally 10.

Reset, set the learning rate back to 0.03, and change "Batch size" from 10 to 30. Watch how many epochs pass between visible changes: each update now averages more examples, and there are fewer updates per epoch.
questions: What happens to the loss when the learning rate is too small? Too large?
In which direction does each update move a weight, relative to the gradient of the loss?
What changes when the batch size is larger?

tasks.title: Back-propagation
steps: Press the step button (▶|) once and look at the connection lines: their thickness and colour show the weights.
Step several more times. Every weight in every layer changes at each step, including the first layer's.
questions: How can the first layer's weights receive an error signal when the error is only measured at the output?

tasks.title: XOR needs a hidden layer
steps: The network has no hidden layer. Play for 300 epochs and note the test loss.
Reset, add a hidden layer with 4 neurons (+ above the hidden layers), and play again.
questions: Why can a network with no hidden layer not solve XOR, while one hidden layer can?

tasks.title: Convolutional networks
steps: TensorFlow Playground cannot show convolutional networks. Read the CNN pages that follow this sheet.
questions: What does one 3×3 kernel compute at one position of an image?
What does 2×2 max pooling do, and does it have weights?

tasks.title: Deep networks and vanishing gradients
steps: Play for 300 epochs with the sigmoid activation and watch how little the first layers' weights change.
Reset, switch the activation to ReLU, and play again.
questions: Why do the earliest layers of a deep sigmoid network learn so slowly?
